newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Dunaholding sees more business in Belgium.
newsitem.headline: Dunaholding sees more business in Belgium.

text.p: Hungarian financial consultant company Dunaholding Rt said on Thursday that it will open its new business centre in Brussels next Wednesday with the aim of boosting east-west relations, and not only on business grounds.

"In addition to the business activity, we regard it as very important to introduce Hungary, including its culture, to the outside world" Andras Meszaros, General Director of the new centre Contact Point Hungary, told a news conference on Thursday.
The opening of the new centre, which wishes to provide up-to-date information about Hungary, is an improvement rather than a start by Dunaholding in Belgium.
"With the establishment of Contact Point Hungary, a new phase starts in Dunaholding's life," Meszaros said.

In 1994 Dunaholding set up Dunaholding Belgique S.A., a wholly-owned unit to help Hungarian companies to do business in the European Union by providing them with more information on public procurement tenders there.
The Belgian unit, which was set up with 50 million Belgian francs share capital, also represented Hungarian companies and products in western Europe and tried to attract foreign investors to Hungary.
Contact Point Hungary, costs of which were covered by Dunaholding Belgique, not only wishes to fulfil all these jobs but wants to widen them as well, he said.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Dunaholding shares ended at 7,300 forints on September 6, the last day when deals were struck on them.
